info.bio: La banda punk-ska The Mighty Mighty Bosstones se formó en 1985 en Boston, EE.UU., y en 1989 lanzó su álbum debut “Devil’s Night Out”. Aunque nunca lograron llegar al mercado comercial, el grupo encabezó el cambio del ska a un genero híbrido de fiesta high-energy, al añadir elementos del pop y el metal. En contraste con la mayoría de bandas de su tipo, los Bosstones mantuvieron algo de la propuesta política del ska, presentándose a menudo para causas locales.

scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.

mentions.text: …akin to girl-groups of the Sixties than hardcore of the Nineties, particularly on Lockjaw (1995). The phenomenon was also pioneered in Boston by Mighty Mighty Bosstones, who penned amusing collections such as Question The Answers (1994). Elsewhere, Wisconsin's Less Than Jake delivered the explosive Pezcore (1994);…

podcast.title: Mighty Mighty Bosstones – Formed 1983 Boston; Invented Skacore by Mixing Two-Tone with Hardcore; Major Label by 1993
podcast.body: The Mighty Mighty Bosstones came together in 1983 when a group of guys became obsessed with the Two-Tone sound despite some members playing in hardcore bands influenced by Motorhead and AC/DC. This combination of Two-Tone ska with American hardcore became known as skacore — annoying to ska purists and initially baffling to hardcore kids, but eventually it clicked. By 1993 they had a major label record deal and a signature look involving plaid suits. "The Boss Tones took two-tone style Skah and made it with American hardcore to create something that was eventually called Skahcore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: A Not-So Brief History of Ska: Part 2

podcast.title: Booked for Content Pivot (1996)
podcast.body: The Mighty Mighty Bosstones were booked for the 1996 Warped Tour as the festival shifted its focus to punk and skate culture-compatible music after securing Vans as a sponsor. "This meant booking fishbone, the muddy, muddy boss tones, no effect, 3-11 penny wise, and this weird new group from San Diego called Blink 182."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Returned for 1997 Tour
podcast.body: The band was among the acts that returned to participate in the Warped Tour in 1997. "Like 1 and 2 was back, as were the boss tones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nate Albert's Membership
podcast.body: Nate Albert, who later became a prominent A&R executive, played guitar for The Mighty Mighty Bosstones. His involvement in the band is mentioned in the context of his A&R career. "Nate is a former member of the mighty, mighty boss tones. He played guitar on songs like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Third Wave Pioneers
podcast.body: Formed in 1983 in Boston, The Mighty Mighty Bosstones were early practitioners of the third wave of Ska, initially inspired by the Two Tone movement but also incorporating hard rock influences from bands like ACDC, Motorhead, and Social Distortion. They became prominent in the late 1980s and early 1990s by fusing Ska with hardcore elements. "The Mighty Mighty Boss Tones. They were formed in 1983 and inspired by the whole two-tone thing, at least originally."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Third Wave Ska Band
podcast.body: The Mighty Mighty Bosstones were identified as a band from the "third wave" of Ska, which arrived in the 1990s. This wave saw significant popularity with bands like No Doubt, Sublime, Reel Big Fish, Goldfinger, and Dance Hall Crashers. "Third wave Scott arrived in the 1990s, no doubt, muddy, muddy boss tones, sublime, real big fish, gold finger, dancehall crashes and so many more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

xref.title: Band Origins and Early Gigs
xref.body: The band was formed in Massachusetts in 1996. Their initial performances took place in the basement of a barber shop. They significantly developed their sound and presence after touring with The Mighty Mighty Bosstones, another band from the Boston area. "Their first gigs were in the basement of a barber shop, but after the muddy, muddy boss tones, another Boston area band, took them on tour, they really came into their own."
